fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for a Finance Team
fields.features_subheading: Each check runs against the systems your team already keeps, and every miss reaches a named owner before month end.
fields.feature_1:
Rules written the way you would say them

Describe a check in a sentence, such as a balance floor or an approval limit. Emergent builds the app, its database and its logic from that prompt, and a new prompt changes a rule.
fields.feature_2:
Your ledger and bank data, connected

The app connects to QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Stripe, and any other tool with an API, and syncs data both ways. Balances and entries come straight from the records your team keeps.
fields.feature_3:
AI that reads invoices and statements

An AI step reads uploaded invoices and bank statements into fields such as the amount and the payee. A field the AI is unsure of goes to a person on your team before a check uses it.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders that move up when unanswered

Each exception reaches its owner in Slack or by email. You set the day a reminder goes out and how long an item can sit unanswered before it moves to the owner's manager.
fields.feature_5:
One live board for open exceptions

The dashboard updates as balances and requests change, with every record saved in a database you own. Month-end review starts from rows the app already stored, not a spreadsheet.
fields.feature_6:
The finance app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can read each rule and review every change to it, the same way they review other code.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Finance Checks That Run on Their Own
fields.tab_content_1:
Operating cash dips under its $250,000 floor

At 7:00 every morning the app reads balances from Quarrybrook Cycle Co.'s 3 bank accounts and posts the total to the finance dashboard: $1,284,600 today. The operating account holds $186,400, under the $250,000 floor set for it. Elliot Pellegarde, the controller, gets a direct message with the balance and the floor.
fields.tab_content_2:
The close waits on a $4,500 gap between companies

Quarrybrook's two companies, Manufacturing and Retail, bill each other monthly. Before the October close, Manufacturing shows $96,300 due from Retail, and Retail shows $91,800 owed. The $4,500 gap holds both closes until the accountants, Brunhild Rasku and Tomas Fontanez, explain it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any credit memo over $1,000 waits for the controller

Requests from outside finance arrive through one form, where the sender picks a type such as a refund or a credit memo. This week 23 came in. Corin Drummellier in sales asked for a $2,400 credit memo for a bike dealer. Because it is over $1,000, it sits with the controller, Elliot Pellegarde, until he approves it.
fields.tab_content_4:
On business day 5, two of nine forecasts are missing

Department heads at Quarrybrook update their next-quarter forecast in a short form by business day 5 each month. This month 7 of the 9 arrived on time. The app emailed 2 reminders, to the heads of Marketing and Facilities, and the dashboard marks both departments as missing for Benedek Szalo, the FP&A lead.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn manual finance checks into finance automation, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the checks done by hand
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give each rule a number and owner
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Connect the ledger and bank data
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the app in one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every check and request finance handles in a month, with who does it and how often. Mark each one that follows a fixed rule with a number in it. Automate those first, and leave anything that needs judgment for later.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Every rule needs a threshold and a person. Write the floor for each bank account and the credit memo amount that needs the controller. Next to each, name the role that acts when the rule fires, not the person who holds it today.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect your accounting system and the other tools the checks read from through their APIs, such as QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite. The app then reads balances and entries at the source instead of from an export someone emails each morning.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the checks, their thresholds and their owners in plain English, along with the request form and the dashboard you want. Emergent builds the app and its database from that prompt. Read the rules back once before you test anything.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick one channel per alert: a Slack direct message for anything the controller must act on today, and email for reminders. Then choose how many hours an alert waits for a reply before the manager of its owner sees it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Load last month's balances and requests, and run every check against them. Compare what the app flags with what your team caught by hand. A check that flags too much needs a tighter threshold, and one that misses a known problem needs a new rule.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Turn on one check at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Switch on the cash check first and keep the others in test for one cycle. Add the next check once the first has run a full month without a false alert. At each month end, open the dashboard to see which checks fired and who closed them.

plan.angle: The top 10 are vendor guides and suites that define finance automation in general terms. This page shows four finance-team automations beyond the ledger work that sibling pages own, drawn as working screens at one company, Quarrybrook Cycle Co.: a 7:00 AM cash check across 3 bank accounts that flags the operating account under its $250,000 floor, an intercompany check that holds the October close over a $4,500 gap, one intake form for finance requests where any credit memo over $1,000 goes to the controller, and forecast updates from 9 department heads with reminders to the 2 still missing. The FAQ answers the example, setup, close, entity and cost questions builders compare.
tab_stories: At 7:00 AM the app reads balances from Quarrybrook's 3 bank accounts, totals $1,284,600, and because the operating account sits at $186,400, under its $250,000 floor, it sends controller Elliot Pellegarde a direct message with the balance.

Before the October close, the app compares the balances the two Quarrybrook companies hold with each other: Manufacturing shows $96,300 due from Retail, Retail shows $91,800 owed, and the $4,500 gap holds both closes until accountants Brunhild Rasku and Tomas Fontanez explain it.

Teams outside finance send refunds, cost center requests and credit memos through one form; 23 came in this week, and a $2,400 credit memo from sales rep Corin Drummellier goes to the controller because any credit memo over $1,000 needs him.

By business day 5 each month, 9 department heads update their next-quarter forecast in a form; 7 are in, the app reminds the heads of Marketing and Facilities, and FP&A lead Benedek Szalo sees the 2 departments marked missing on the dashboard.
